compute.cost_note: stdlib only; one read and strip pass per file; wall-clock grows with file count (seconds at 10K files, about 30 min at 436K)

do_not_use_when: you need schema or provenance checks (use manifest_validator)
the manifest exceeds about 1M files (use shard_runner --task corpus_hygiene; the script warns at that size)
you want a prose-quality, authorship or AI/human judgment; the ratio only measures strippable non-prose content

examples.description: Hygiene-check the baseline slice of a manifest

inputs.target: files (--path), directories of .txt/.md (--dir), or a JSONL manifest (--manifest, optionally --filter)

artifacts: JSON report with per-file strip ratios and statuses (--json)

purpose: Content-level corpus hygiene gate. Runs the preprocessing strip rules over files, directories, or a filtered manifest slice and reports, per file, the share of tokens stripped as suspected non-prose contamination (HTML, CSS, code, tables, markup) that would distort POS/KL and other distributional diagnostics; files are clean, warn (>= 1% stripped) or fail (>= 5%) at operator-adjustable thresholds, and undecodable bytes are counted.
use_when: before a KL-sensitive diagnostic, baseline build, or validation_harness run, to refuse contaminated inputs
checking newly acquired impostor or baseline text for scraped markup or code
auditing a manifest slice (--manifest with --filter use=baseline,register=...)
